{
  "candidate_rtl": "module comparator_16bit (
    input [15:0] A,
    input [15:0] B,
    output gt,
    output eq,
    output lt
);
    wire [15:0] same;
    wire [15:0] greater_bit;
    wire [3:0] group_equal;
    wire [3:0] group_greater;

    assign same = ~(A ^ B);
    assign greater_bit = A & ~B;

    genvar k;
    generate
        for (k = 0; k < 4; k = k + 1) begin : groups
            assign group_equal[k] = &same[4*k +: 4];
            assign group_greater[k] =
                greater_bit[4*k+3] |
                (same[4*k+3] & greater_bit[4*k+2]) |
                (same[4*k+3] & same[4*k+2] & greater_bit[4*k+1]) |
                (same[4*k+3] & same[4*k+2] & same[4*k+1] & greater_bit[4*k]);
        end
    endgenerate

    assign gt = group_greater[3] |
                (group_equal[3] & group_greater[2]) |
                (group_equal[3] & group_equal[2] & group_greater[1]) |
                (group_equal[3] & group_equal[2] & group_equal[1] & group_greater[0]);
    assign eq = &group_equal;
    assign lt = ~(gt | eq);
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The baseline's worst reported path reaches gt at 0.88 ns through comparison and output-combination logic. Its equality output also depends on a relatively late mapped comparison path.",
  "rewrite": "Use four parallel four-bit priority comparisons followed by an explicit four-group lookahead comparison. Share bit-equality terms, compute equality independently, and derive lt from the mutually exclusive unsigned greater-than and equality results.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The bounded lookahead structure targets reduced comparison depth relative to the 0.88 ns baseline. Actual improvement requires mapping and STA; the final NOR producing lt may become the limiting output.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Shared equality terms and elimination of a separate less-than comparator limit duplication. The intended area is below the 547.775360 um2 cap, but mapped area and zero slew/capacitance violations require verification in the specified flow.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module name and all unsigned 16-bit input and scalar output ports. For every binary input pair, gt means A>B, eq means A==B, and lt means A<B. No parameters, state, latency, assumptions, dependencies, or undefined outputs are introduced."
}
